seoTitle: How to Autofill Jotform Fields Using Excel Data
metaDescription: Learn how to use the Jotform Spreadsheet to Form widget in 2026 to pre-populate form fields from an Excel file using a unique access code.
intro: Manually re-entering client details or order history into a form frustrates users and slows things down, but Jotform's Spreadsheet to Form widget can autofill fields from your existing Excel data. This guide covers preparing your spreadsheet with an access code column, uploading it to the widget, and mapping the columns to your form fields.

steps.heading: Structure your Excel spreadsheet
steps.body: Add a unique access code identifier column to your spreadsheet so each row can be matched cleanly to a form field lookup.

steps.heading: Add the widget to your form
steps.body: Open the widgets sidebar in your form builder and add the Spreadsheet to Form widget to your canvas.

steps.heading: Upload your Excel file
steps.body: Upload your prepared .xlsx file directly into the widget's configuration panel.

steps.heading: Set the access code column and map fields
steps.body: Set the primary access code column parameter, then map spreadsheet column headers to the corresponding form input fields.

steps.heading: Customize and test the autofill flow
steps.body: Adjust the access code input box and verification button design, then test the live autofill sequence on both desktop and mobile.

faq.question: What file formats does the Spreadsheet to Form widget accept?
faq.answer: The widget is built around Excel spreadsheet files, so preparing your data as a properly structured .xlsx file is the standard approach.

faq.question: Can users autofill multiple fields with one access code?
faq.answer: Yes, entering a single unique access code can populate several mapped fields at once, such as name, address, and order history.

faq.question: Does this widget work on mobile forms?
faq.answer: Yes, testing the live autofill sequence on both desktop and mobile is a recommended step to confirm it renders correctly everywhere.

faq.question: What happens if a user enters an access code that isn't in the spreadsheet?
faq.answer: The widget won't find a matching row, so the autofill fields simply won't populate, and the form typically remains fillable manually.
